findings.title: A response the cdp parser rejects kills the listener and leaves send() hanging forever
findings.scenario: tab.send(cmd) or any helper built on it (tab.evaluate, get_cookies, update_targets, get_frames). Chrome's reply has a shape the generated parser does not accept: a required field is missing or an enum value is newer than the generated protocol (Chrome version skew). The Listener pops the tx from mapper and calls tx(**message) at listener_loop line 973. Transaction.__call__ catches only StopIteration around self.__cdp_obj__.send(response['result']), so the KeyError or ValueError from from_json propagates out of __call__ and out of listener_loop. The future is never resolved. The same happens if 'result' is missing (KeyError) and on the explicit `raise ProtocolException('could not parse...')` at line 130. Result: the awaiting send() hangs with no timeout, and the listener task dies. Other in-flight commands on that connection also hang until some later send() starts a new Listener. For a session tab, events pile up in the unbounded _inbox with nothing reading them.
findings.why_tests_miss: Tests run against the Chrome build that matches the generated protocol, so parsing never fails. tests/core/test_connection.py's FakeWebSocket answers only Target.setDiscoverTargets, whose parser ignores the result. The known listener-exception lead is about exceptions from _receive_message inside the try block. tx(**message) is outside that try, so widening that except would not fix this: __call__ itself needs to set_exception on the future.
findings.repro_idea: Run a fake websockets peer that answers Target.getTargetInfo with {"id":N,"result":{}}, or Storage.getCookies with a cookie whose sameSite is 'SomeFutureValue'. Then call asyncio.wait_for(conn.send(cdp.target.get_target_info()), 3), which times out, and check that conn.listener.task.exception() is the KeyError or ValueError.
findings.evidence: probe_parse.py against a fake CDP peer printed: 'send() HUNG (timed out after 3s) / listener done: True exception: KeyError('targetInfo') / mapper after: {}'. For the cookie: 'send() HUNG ... listener done: True exception: ValueError("'SomeFutureValue' is not a valid CookieSameSite")'. A later send worked only because send() recreates the dead listener.

findings.title: Browser.stop() right after Chrome dies raises ConnectionClosedError from Tab.aclose and leaks the process and temp profile
findings.bug_class: incomplete exception handling on close path
findings.scenario: browser = await zd.start(); tab = await browser.get(...); await tab.evaluate('1') (the tab now has a flat session). Chrome crashes or is killed (OOM, watchdog, browser._process.kill()), and then await browser.stop() runs before the listener has seen the close. Browser._stop calls target.aclose() for every tab. The session branch of aclose sends Target.detachFromTarget and catches only ProtocolException. The listener's ConnectionClosed branch fails pending transactions with the ConnectionClosed instance itself (_fail_pending_transactions(e)), and _send_transaction can also raise ConnectionClosed directly. Either way ConnectionClosedError escapes aclose and aborts Browser._stop before the browser.close send (whose broad except would have handled it), before proxy forwarders are closed, before the process is terminated/reaped (browser._process stays set) and before _cleanup_temporary_profile. stop() has already unregistered the atexit cleanup, so the temp profile dir is never removed. A second problem on the same line: the detach round trip has no timeout. With a frozen Chrome (SIGSTOP), stop() hangs inside Tab.aclose (stack: stop -> _stop:879 -> aclose:517 -> send:662) and never reaches the terminate/kill fallback. Before #280, tab.aclose only closed a per-tab websocket.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_browser_stop_can_be_called_on_a_closed_connection closes browser.connection first, so all sessions are already detached and no round trip happens. test_browser_stopped_is_true_when_stopped_externally never calls stop() right after a crash. No test kills Chrome and then calls stop() while a tab session is attached.
findings.repro_idea: browser = await zd.start(headless=True); tab = await browser.get('about:blank'); await tab.evaluate('1'); browser._process.kill(); await browser.stop() raises ConnectionClosedError; then check os.path.exists(browser.config.user_data_dir).
findings.evidence: probe_stop_after_crash.py on real headless Chromium printed 'stop RAISED ConnectionClosedError no close frame received or sent | _process still set: True | profile dir still exists: True' in 5 of 5 runs. Traceback: browser.py stop 872 -> _stop 879 -> connection.py aclose 517 -> send 662 -> (exception originated in) listener_loop 925. With a 0.5s sleep between kill and stop, stop succeeds because the listener had already detached the sessions. probe_stop_frozen.py (SIGSTOP) showed stop() still pending after 5s, awaiting inside aclose:517.

findings.title: NaN or Infinity in any command param makes the command hang forever (invalid JSON, id-less error reply)
findings.scenario: tab.send(cdp.emulation.set_device_metrics_override(width=100, height=100, device_scale_factor=float('nan'), mobile=False)). The same applies to tab.mouse_move(float('inf'), 10), or to runtime.call_function_on with CallArgument(value=float('nan')) (for example numpy data). Transaction.message calls json.dumps with the default allow_nan=True, so the frame contains the bare tokens NaN or Infinity, which are not valid JSON. Chrome cannot parse the frame and replies {"error":{"code":-32700,"message":"JSON: invalid token at position N"}} with no id. The listener treats a message without 'id' as an event. parse_json_event fails, the failure is logged at INFO, and the loop continues. The tx stays in mapper and send() never returns. The fix is to serialize with allow_nan=False, which raises ValueError inside _send_transaction's try; that path already pops the tx.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test passes non-finite floats. The only fake-websocket test replies to every command by id and never sees an id-less error.
findings.repro_idea: On real Chrome: asyncio.wait_for(tab.send(cdp.emulation.set_device_metrics_override(width=100,height=100,device_scale_factor=float('nan'),mobile=False)), 4) raises TimeoutError, and tab.mapper still holds the id.
findings.evidence: probe_nan2.py on real headless Chromium printed 'send HUNG 4s; pending tab.mapper: [9]' and the only frame received was 'recv: {"error":{"code":-32700,"message":"JSON: invalid token at position 110"}}' (no id). The connection was still usable afterwards (evaluate('2+2') -> 4), so only that command is lost.

findings.title: One ProtocolException instance is shared by all pending commands, and each send() appends its own command to it
findings.scenario: Several commands are in flight on one connection (for example asyncio.gather of browser.connection.send(get_targets()), send(create_target(url='https://secret.example/?token=abc')) and send(get_version())), or on one tab session. Then the connection is closed (aclose) or the session is detached (_detach_session: tab closed, or browser connection closed). _fail_pending_transactions sets the same exception object on every pending tx. In send(), `e.message += f"\ncommand:{tx.method}\nparams:{tx.params}"` then mutates that shared instance once per waiter. Every caller gets the identical object, and its str() lists the commands and params of all the other callers. The error for get_targets shows createTarget's URL, token included. The traceback is also re-raised from several tasks.

findings.title: A successful session reply that arrives in the same burst as Target.detachedFromTarget is discarded and the caller gets 'target session was detached'
findings.scenario: tab.send(cmd) on a flat session where the command makes the target go away (closing a page or popup through its own session, an OOPIF disappearing), or a reply and the detach that are simply buffered together under load. The browser listener routes the reply into session._inbox with put_nowait. It then reads the next buffered frame without yielding, because wait_for awaits the coroutine inline and websockets returns buffered frames immediately. That frame is Target.detachedFromTarget, so _receive_message calls session._detach_session(). That sets self._inbox = None, which drops the queued reply, and fails every pending tx with ProtocolException('target session was detached'). The command succeeded in Chrome, but the caller sees a failure. The comment in Tab.close ('sent through the browser session, since this tab's own session may be detached before chrome responds') works around exactly this for close_target, but every other session command is still exposed. A fix would drain the inbox (or deliver the detach through the inbox) before failing the pending txs.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_tab_session_is_detached_when_tab_closes only checks state after the close, and Tab.close avoids the race by using the browser session. With real Chrome the reply and the detach usually arrive in separate reads, so the window is timing-dependent and no test sends them back-to-back.
findings.repro_idea: Run a fake peer whose Runtime.evaluate handler sends the reply (with sessionId) and then immediately Target.detachedFromTarget for that session. tab.send(runtime.evaluate('1+1')) then raises ProtocolException. Adding a 50ms gap between the two frames makes it succeed.
findings.evidence: probe_detach_race.py (owner stub plus session Connection, unique session id per attach) printed 'evaluate replied successfully by chrome: 20; caller saw success: 0, saw ProtocolException: 20 / example error: target session was detached'. The control probe_detach_race_delay.py, with a 50ms gap between reply and detach, printed 'caller saw success: 20, saw ProtocolException: 0'. On real Chromium with page.close / target.close via the session, the frames arrived separately in 6 trials, so the bug did not show there.

findings.title: Cancelling the first command on a fresh tab during attach leaks a Chrome-side CDP session that is never detached
findings.scenario: tab = await browser.get(url, new_tab=True) (the tab is not attached yet). Then asyncio.wait_for(tab.evaluate('1+1'), small_timeout), or any timeout or cancel that hits the first send. _attach_session has already sent Target.attachToTarget and is awaiting the reply when it is cancelled. Chrome creates the session, but self.session_id is never set and the id is never recorded in browser_connection._sessions. The next send attaches a second session. tab.aclose() and Browser.stop() later detach only the recorded session, so the orphaned DevTools session stays attached in Chrome until the browser websocket closes. Each timed-out first command leaks one.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test cancels or times out a command on a not-yet-attached tab. The known mapper lead is about the leftover Transaction, not about the Chrome-side session it creates.
findings.repro_idea: On real Chrome, add handlers for target.AttachedToTarget and DetachedFromTarget on browser.connection. Open a new tab, time out its first evaluate after 2ms, evaluate again, call tab.aclose(), then compare the attached and detached session ids.
findings.evidence: probe_orphan_session.py on real headless Chromium printed 'tab session after timeout: None attached events so far: [SessionID('0784...')]', then 'attached: [0784..., F341...]', 'detached after tab.aclose(): [F341...]', 'orphan sessions (attached, never detached): [SessionID('078467FA91818147B95CF37E0B413ABE')]'.

findings.title: remove_handlers(module, handler) silently does nothing after add_handler(module, handler)
findings.scenario: tab.add_handler(cdp.network, h) is documented ('if event_type_or_domain is a module ... it will find all available events and add the handler') and registers h under each of the 44 cdp.network event classes. The natural inverse, tab.remove_handlers(cdp.network, h) or tab.remove_handlers(cdp.network), looks up self.handlers[cdp.network] (or pops it). That key never exists, so nothing is removed and no error is raised. h keeps firing on every network event, and the Network domain stays auto-enabled. The only ways to undo the add are to remove each of the 44 event classes by hand or to clear every handler with remove_handlers().
findings.why_tests_miss: tests/core/test_tab.py's remove_handlers tests use only event classes (cdp.network.RequestWillBeSent), never a module.
findings.repro_idea: conn.add_handler(cdp.network, h); conn.remove_handlers(cdp.network, h); then count the handler lists that still contain h. Expected 0, actual 44.
findings.evidence: probe_handlers.py printed 'event types with h after add_handler(cdp.network, h): 44', 'after remove_handlers(cdp.network, h): 44', 'after remove_handlers(cdp.network): 44'. Confidence is medium only because remove_handlers is annotated Optional[type], although add_handler explicitly accepts modules.

findings.scenario: tab.send(cdp.page.navigate(url=None)), or any call that sends bad params. findings.title: Chrome's stdout/stderr are PIPEs that are never drained: once ~64 KiB of logs pile up, Chrome blocks and every CDP call (and stop()) hangs
findings.scenario: zd.start() spawns Chrome with stdout=PIPE and stderr=PIPE. Nothing reads them during the session; only _read_process_stderr does, and only after start() fails to connect. Chrome logs ERROR lines to stderr. Default flags in a container already leave about 5 KB at startup (dbus errors), and each navigation that hits a certificate error adds about 370 bytes. When the 64 KiB kernel pipe buffer fills, the Chrome thread that logs blocks in write(2). From then on: (a) default flags: after about 157 bad-certificate navigations, Page.navigate is never answered, so tab.get / tab.send / find etc. hang; (b) with a common debugging flag such as browser_args=['--enable-logging=stderr','--v=1'], the browser process stops answering even Browser.getVersion within a few navigations, and browser.stop() hangs too (see the stop() finding). The user sees a browser that just stops responding, with no error.
findings.why_tests_miss: The tests are short sessions that never produce 64 KiB of Chrome logs. test_connection_error_raises_exception_and_logs_stderr only checks that 'Browser stderr' gets logged after a mocked connection failure.
findings.repro_idea: Start with browser_args=['--enable-logging=stderr','--v=1'], loop over tab.get(data-url) with a 10 s wait_for, and observe the TimeoutError after about 5 iterations while FIONREAD on browser._process.stderr reads about 64 KiB. Fix: spawn with stdout/stderr=DEVNULL (or a file / a drained reader task) and keep only a bounded tail for the failure message.

In normal navigation without errors (probe_pipe.py, default flags, 400 pages) stderr stayed at 5019 bytes, so the growth comes from Chrome's ERROR logging.

findings.title: Browser.stop() waits on unbounded CDP replies before it kills the process, so an unresponsive browser makes stop() hang forever and leaks the process
findings.scenario: When the browser process stops answering (e.g. the stderr-pipe deadlock above, a wedged or suspended Chrome, a remote browser that hangs), await browser.stop() never returns. _stop first runs `await target.aclose()` for every target. For each attached flat session that does `await browser_connection.send(Target.detachFromTarget)` with no timeout. It then does `await self.connection.send(cdp.browser.close())`, also with no timeout. Only after both does it reach the terminate -> 3 s -> kill fallback, which is the code meant for an unresponsive browser. If the caller bounds stop() with asyncio.wait_for, the process is never terminated and the temp profile is never removed. stop() already called asyncio_atexit.unregister(self._atexit_cleanup) and discarded the instance from the registry before awaiting _stop(), so nothing cleans up at exit either. Tab.close() has the same shape: its `await self.browser.connection.send(close_target)` sits outside the `asyncio.wait_for(future, 10)` that its ':raises asyncio.TimeoutError:' docstring promises.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_pending_commands_fail_when_browser_process_dies and test_pending_commands_fail_when_connection_is_closed suspend Chrome, but they kill or resume it before stop() runs. No test calls stop() while the browser is unresponsive.
findings.repro_idea: browser = await zd.start(headless=True); tab = await browser.get(url); await tab.evaluate('1') to attach a session; os.kill(pid, SIGSTOP); then assert asyncio.wait_for(browser.stop(), 20) completes and the process is gone. Fix: bound the detach/Browser.close steps (e.g. wait_for of a few seconds each, or overall) and always fall through to terminate/kill.

findings.title: An exception while parsing a command response kills the Listener without failing the Transaction, so the awaiting send() hangs forever
findings.scenario: Any send() whose response fails parsing in Transaction.__call__ hangs forever. Causes include a generated from_json KeyError/ValueError (protocol drift, an unknown enum value) or a custom command generator as allowed by the send() docstring. Example: `def cmd(): j = yield {'method':'Runtime.evaluate','params':{'expression':'1'}}; return j['x']`, then `await tab.send(cmd())` never returns. `tx(**message)` runs outside every try block. The exception escapes listener_loop, the task dies with 'Task exception was never retrieved', and tx (already popped from mapper) is never set_result/set_exception'd. Any concurrent tab.wait() blocked on that listener's idle event also hangs. This is a different site from the known issue: that issue covers the try around _receive_message, and here the receive succeeded and the response dispatch is what fails.
findings.why_tests_miss: Tests only use well-formed Chrome responses, and the FakeWebSocket in test_connection.py answers {'result': {}} to set_discover_targets, which returns None with no parsing. Event parse failures are caught and logged, but response parse failures are never exercised.

The fix is to wrap tx(**message) and set_exception on the tx.

findings.title: Once the browser connection's Listener stops, every flat-session Tab command hangs because the tab path never restarts the parent listener

For a Tab, aopen() calls only _attach_session(), which returns early when session_id is set and never calls browser_connection.aopen(). send() then restarts only the tab's own Listener, which reads tab._inbox. findings.scenario: (a) feed_cdp's docstring presents it as the non-async way to answer cdp.fetch.RequestPaused. That call raises RuntimeError('Executor shutdown has been called'). Only ProcessLookupError is caught, so `_cleanup_temporary_profile()` never runs, either inside `_stop` or after it in `_atexit_cleanup`. findings.title: Restarting a stopped or crashed Browser never relaunches Chrome: stop() leaves config.host/port set, so start() takes the connect-existing path
findings.scenario: `b = await zd.start(); await b.stop(); await b.start()`. The first start() wrote host='127.0.0.1' and port=free_port() into self.config. stop() clears _process and _process_pid but not host or port. So the second start() sees host and port both set and sets connect_existing=True: no executable check, no process spawn. test_connection then fails every retry against the dead port. The `if not self.info` check uses the stale self.info from the first run instead of the `connected` flag, so the clear 'Failed to connect' error is skipped. Connection(stale ws url).send(...) then raises ConnectionRefusedError. The crash case is broken too: when the process died, start() calls `self.create(config=self.config)`, which copies the same host/port into a new instance, and that instance fails with 'Failed to connect to browser'. Even with host/port reset by hand, stop() leaves the old Tab objects in self.targets, so tabs[0] is a dead target and browser.get() fails with 'No target with given id found'. A restarted browser is also never registered with asyncio_atexit again, because only create() registers it.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test calls start() on a Browser that has been stopped or has crashed. The tests only check `stopped` after stop() or after an external kill.
findings.repro_idea: `b = await zd.start(headless=True); await b.stop(); await b.start()` raises ConnectionRefusedError after about 2.5 s. `b._process.kill(); b._process.wait(); await b.start()` raises 'Failed to connect to browser'.

Failed to connect to browser ...]'. probe_restart2.py, with host/port reset by hand: 'first tab is stale: True' and 'get after restart raised ProtocolException No target with given id found command:Target.attachToTarget'.

findings.title: Cancelling or failing Browser.start after Chrome is spawned orphans the Chrome process, its temp profile and the registry entry
findings.scenario: `await asyncio.wait_for(zd.start(), 2)` times out on a slow machine. The same happens with Ctrl+C during startup (asyncio.run cancels main) or task.cancel() on shutdown. start() has already spawned Chrome at util._start_process and added self to util.get_registered_instances(). The CancelledError, or any exception after the spawn (from set_discover_targets, update_targets or _read_headless_user_agent), leaves start() with no try/finally. Browser.create registers asyncio_atexit only after start() returns, so no atexit cleanup exists, and the caller never gets the instance to call stop() on. The Chrome process keeps running after the Python interpreter exits (reparented to pid 1). The /tmp/uc_* profile is never removed. The registry set holds the Browser forever.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test cancels or times out zd.start()/Browser.create. The only start-failure test (test_connection_error_raises_exception_and_logs_stderr) goes through the `not self.info` branch, which does call stop().
findings.repro_idea: Run `asyncio.run(...)` with `await asyncio.wait_for(zd.start(headless=True), 0.05)` inside try/except TimeoutError. Then check psutil.pid_exists() for the pid of the instance left in util.get_registered_instances(), and look for /tmp/uc_* dirs. Check again after the interpreter exits with `ps -o ppid`.
findings.evidence: probe_cancel_start.py with timeouts 0.05 and 0.15: 'start timed out', 'registered instances: 1', 'pid 23314 alive True info False connection None', 'new temp profiles left: {/tmp/uc_jqua_ubs}', 'pid 23314 running after asyncio.run: running'. After the script exited, `ps` showed pids 23314 and 23411 with ppid 1, still running. I killed them by hand.

findings.title: Browser.stop() hangs forever on an unresponsive browser and never reaches terminate()/kill()
findings.scenario: The Chrome process is wedged: frozen, stopped, or blocked writing to its full stderr pipe (see the pipe finding). `await browser.stop()` first runs `for target in self.targets: await target.aclose()`, and each aclose sends Target.detachFromTarget over the browser connection with no timeout. Next comes `await self.connection.send(cdp.browser.close())`, also with no timeout. The websocket stays open but no reply ever arrives, so stop() blocks forever. The terminate/kill block, which exists to handle a stubborn process, is never reached. The obvious workaround, `asyncio.wait_for(browser.stop(), t)`, makes things worse: stop() has already unregistered the atexit callback and removed the instance from the registry before awaiting _stop(), so after the timeout nothing will ever kill Chrome or remove the temp profile.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_pending_commands_fail_when_browser_process_dies suspends the process but then kills it before checking anything. No test calls stop() while the browser is unresponsive.
findings.repro_idea: `b = await zd.start(headless=True); await b.get('about:blank'); os.kill(b._process_pid, SIGSTOP); t = asyncio.create_task(b.stop()); await asyncio.wait({t}, timeout=12)`. t is still pending and t.print_stack() shows it waiting on the Target.detachFromTarget Transaction.
findings.evidence: probe_stop_hang.py printed 'stop() still running after 12s; stuck at: Stack for <Task pending ... coro=<Browser.stop() running at browser.py:872> wait_for=<Transaction method: Target.detachFromTarget status: pending>>' and 'process still alive: True'. probe_pipe2.py: `wait_for(b.stop(), 20)` timed out for a browser blocked on stderr.

findings.title: Chrome's stdout/stderr are PIPEs that are never drained; once 64 KiB is written Chrome blocks and every CDP command hangs
findings.scenario: `zd.start(browser_args=['--enable-logging=stderr'])` (or `--v=1`, or a build or flags that log a lot), then run a page that logs to the console. Browser.start launches Chrome with stdout=PIPE and stderr=PIPE, and nothing reads them while the browser runs. _read_process_stderr only reads on a failed start. When the kernel pipe buffer fills (64 KiB on Linux), Chrome's write(2) on stderr blocks and the browser stops answering CDP. tab.evaluate('1+1') never returns, and browser.stop() hangs too (see the stop() finding). Default flags write only about 5 KB at startup in this environment, so the trigger needs logging enabled or a chatty build.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test passes logging flags or produces stderr output; sessions are short and stay far below 64 KiB.
findings.repro_idea: Start with browser_args=['--enable-logging=stderr'], run `console.log('x'.repeat(100))` 600 times through tab.evaluate, and watch FIONREAD on b._process.stderr reach about 64 KiB. Then `await asyncio.wait_for(tab.evaluate('1+1'), 10)` raises TimeoutError.
findings.evidence: probe_pipe2.py: 'stderr pending after start: 6124', 'round 0 ok, stderr pending: 56414', 'round 1 TIMEOUT, stderr pending: 64420', 'simple evaluate TIMEOUT: browser hung; pending 64420', 'stop timed out'. probe_pipe.py with default flags: stderr stayed at 5241 bytes after console spam and failed navigations.

findings.title: Browsers made from one Config share a single temp profile once its user_data_dir has been materialized (e.g. by print(config)); a failed browser then deletes the live browser's profile
findings.scenario: `config = zd.Config(headless=True); print(config)` (or `config()`, or reading config.user_data_dir). Then `b1 = await zd.start(config); b2 = await zd.start(config)`. Config.__repr__ calls the user_data_dir property getter, which runs mkdtemp on the template, and _custom_data_dir stays False. Browser.__init__ deep-copies the template, so every browser gets the same temp path and treats it as its own temporary profile. Chrome's process singleton hands b2's launch to b1's process, and b2 fails with 'Failed to connect to browser'. b2's failure path calls stop() -> _cleanup_temporary_profile(), which runs shutil.rmtree on the directory b1 is actively using. Without a failure, the first stop() of either browser deletes the profile of the other, still-running one.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_multiple_browsers_diff_userdata reuses one Config but never touches the template's user_data_dir, repr or __call__ before the browsers start, so each deep copy creates its own lazy temp dir.
findings.repro_idea: `config = zd.Config(headless=True); repr(config); b1 = await zd.start(config)`. Then `zd.start(config)` raises. After that, `os.path.exists(b1.config.user_data_dir)` is False while b1 is still running.
findings.evidence: probe_shared_profile.py: 'template repr touches user_data_dir: True', 'b1 udd /tmp/uc_tjiysmh9', 'b2 failed: Exception [... Failed to connect to browser]', 'b1 still running: True b1 profile dir exists: False'.

findings.title: Every Browser.create that fails before spawning Chrome (e.g. bad browser_executable_path) leaks a temp profile directory
findings.scenario: `await zd.start(browser_executable_path='/nonexistent/chrome')` in a retry loop. Browser.__init__ runs `logger.debug("Session object initialized: %s" % vars(self))`. The % formatting happens even when debug logging is off. It calls Config.__repr__, which calls the user_data_dir getter, which runs mkdtemp. start() then raises FileNotFoundError at the executable check with no cleanup, and create() never returns the instance. Even if the caller held it, stop() -> _stop() returns early (`if not self.connection and not self._process: return`) before _cleanup_temporary_profile. Each failed call leaves one /tmp/uc_* directory behind.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test starts zendriver with a missing executable or any other failure before the spawn.
findings.repro_idea: Call `zd.start(browser_executable_path='/nonexistent/chrome')` three times, catching FileNotFoundError each time, and diff glob('/tmp/uc_*') before and after.
findings.evidence: probe_exe_missing.py: 'temp profiles leaked by 3 failed starts: 3 ['/tmp/uc_6y2b1hkp', '/tmp/uc_jcsk9199', '/tmp/uc_k388terb']'.

findings.title: Browser.__aexit__ rebuilds the exception as exc_type(exc_val): many exceptions turn into TypeError, attributes and traceback are lost, and the browser is never stopped
findings.scenario: `async with await zd.start() as browser:` is the documented pattern in examples/wait_for_page.py. Any exception inside the block goes through `raise exc_type(exc_val)` instead of propagating unchanged. websockets ConnectionClosedError(rcvd, sent) and json.JSONDecodeError(msg, doc, pos) both need more than one constructor argument, so the user gets 'TypeError: ... missing ... required positional argument' instead of the real error. A ProtocolException comes back as a new instance with .code None, and the original traceback is replaced. The `async with` block also never calls stop(), so Chrome keeps running until loop close, where atexit cleanup then fails (see the atexit finding).
findings.why_tests_miss: No test uses `async with` on a Browser. CreateBrowser is a separate context manager that calls stop() itself.
findings.repro_idea: `b = zd.Browser(zd.Config(headless=True))` inside a running loop, then `async with b: raise websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError(None, None)` and check that TypeError is caught. Do the same with ProtocolException({'code': -32000, 'message': 'm'}) and check that e.code is None.
findings.evidence: probe_aexit.py: 'raised ConnectionClosedError -> caught TypeError: ConnectionClosed.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'sent'', 'raised JSONDecodeError -> caught TypeError: JSONDecodeError.__init__() missing 2 required positional arguments', 'raised ProtocolException -> caught ProtocolException: No node with given id found [code: -32000] | code=None'. Connection.__aexit__ in connection.py has the same pattern.

findings.title: Connecting to an existing or remote browser (host+port) fails with FileNotFoundError when no local Chrome is installed
findings.scenario: In a container without Chrome, run `await zd.start(host='chrome-host', port=9222)` against a running DevTools endpoint. Browser.create/util.start build Config(...), and Config.__init__ calls find_executable(browser) whenever browser_executable_path is not given. find_executable raises FileNotFoundError('could not find a valid browser binary'). Browser.start deliberately skips the executable check when connect_existing (`if not connect_existing:` at browser.py:537), but it is never reached. create_from_undetected_chromedriver (`Config()`) fails the same way when Chrome is not in a standard location.
findings.why_tests_miss: The tests always launch a local browser and have Chrome on PATH. No test connects with host/port.
findings.repro_idea: Launch chromium by absolute path with --remote-debugging-port=9557. With PATH not containing any chrome binary, run `await zd.start(host='127.0.0.1', port=9557)` and observe FileNotFoundError.
findings.evidence: probe_remote.py with the default PATH (no chrome): 'zd.start(host, port) raised FileNotFoundError could not find a valid browser binary...'. With chromium on PATH, the same call connects fine.

findings.title: For a host/port-connected Browser, `stopped` is always True and start() is not idempotent: a second start() leaks the first websocket connection and listener
findings.scenario: `b = await zd.start(host='127.0.0.1', port=9222)` attaches to a running browser. `b.stopped` returns True right away, because it only looks at self._process, which is None when connecting. The atexit cleanup therefore skips _stop(). A later `await b.start()` (for example retry or reconnect logic) passes the `if self._process or self._process_pid` guard, because both are None, and builds a new Connection over self.connection without closing the old one. The old websocket and its Listener task stay open for the life of the loop.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test connects to an existing browser via host/port.
findings.repro_idea: Launch chromium by hand on a port and connect with zd.start(host, port). Assert b.stopped is True. Keep `old = b.connection`, call `await b.start()`, then check that `not old.closed and old.listener.running`.
findings.evidence: probe_remote.py with chromium on PATH: 'connected: ws://127.0.0.1:9557/devtools/browser/... stopped property: True' and 'second start(): connection replaced: True old still open: True old listener running: True'.

findings.title: Concurrent Browser.stop() calls race in _stop and raise AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'poll'
findings.scenario: Call stop() from two tasks at once, for example a signal-handler task plus a finally block, or `await asyncio.gather(b.stop(), b.stop())`. Both enter _stop past the `if not self.connection and not self._process` guard and both reach the terminate/poll loop. The first one to see the exit sets `self._process = None` (line 916). The other wakes from `asyncio.sleep(0.25)` and runs `self._process.poll()` or `asyncio.to_thread(self._process.wait)` on None. Its stop() raises AttributeError, and its profile cleanup is skipped.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_browser_stop_can_be_called_multiple_times calls stop() sequentially, never concurrently.
findings.repro_idea: `b = await zd.start(headless=True); await b.get('about:blank'); res = await asyncio.gather(b.stop(), b.stop(), return_exceptions=True)`. Repeat; some runs return an AttributeError.
findings.evidence: probe_concurrent_stop.py over 7 runs: 2 runs printed "results: ['AttributeError(\"'NoneType' object has no attribute 'poll'\")', 'None']" and the other 5 printed ['None', 'None'].

findings.title: Iterating a Browser with no page tabs, nested or after exhaustion crashes; parallel iterators share one cursor
findings.scenario: __iter__ returns self and keeps the cursor in self._i. (a) Close every tab, then call `list(browser)` or `next(iter(browser), None)`: there is no main_tab, so __iter__ never sets _i. __next__ then hits AttributeError, and its handler runs `del self._i`, which raises AttributeError again, so the caller gets AttributeError instead of StopIteration. (b) Only non-page targets remain (e.g. a service worker): main_tab returns that target, and `self.tabs.index(main_tab)` raises ValueError. (c) Nested loops `for a in browser: for b in browser:` crash with AttributeError because the inner loop deletes the shared _i. `zip(browser, browser)` silently returns [(A, B)] instead of [(A, A), (B, B)]. (d) Calling next() again on an exhausted iterator raises AttributeError, which breaks the rule that it must keep raising StopIteration. (e) __reversed__ returns a list, so `next(reversed(browser))` raises TypeError.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test in tests/ iterates a Browser. grep for 'in browser:', 'list(browser', 'iter(browser' and 'reversed(browser' finds nothing.
findings.repro_idea: Inside asyncio.run, build `b = Browser(Config(browser_executable_path='/bin/true'))` and set b.targets by hand with b._create_tab(TargetInfo(...)). Then check list(b) with no targets, list(b) with only a service_worker target, the nested comprehension, zip(b, b), and next(it, None) after list(it). Alternatively start real Chromium, close all tabs, then call list(browser).

With real Chromium (misc_probe.py), after closing all tabs: targets == [] and list(browser) raises AttributeError 'Browser' object has no attribute '_i'.

findings.title: HTTPApi sends the local DevTools /json/version request through the http_proxy env var, so start() fails behind a proxy
findings.scenario: A user has http_proxy (or HTTP_PROXY) set in the environment and no no_proxy entry for 127.0.0.1, as on many corporate machines. They call `await zd.start()`. HTTPApi._request uses urllib.request.urlopen, which uses the default ProxyHandler. That handler sends GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/json/version to the corporate proxy, which cannot reach the user's loopback. Every test_connection attempt fails, and start() stops the browser and raises 'Failed to connect to browser ... you are running as root, pass sandbox=False', even though Chrome started and is listening. (urllib.request.proxy_bypass_environment only skips the proxy when no_proxy is set.)
findings.why_tests_miss: The tests run without http_proxy set. CI and this container set no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1. No test exercises HTTPApi with proxy environment variables.
findings.repro_idea: Start a dummy TCP 'proxy' on 127.0.0.1 that records the request line and answers 502. Remove no_proxy/NO_PROXY from os.environ and set http_proxy to the dummy. Then call `await zd.start(headless=True, browser_connection_max_tries=3)`.
findings.evidence: Probe scratchpad/detect-A4/proxy_probe.py printed 'start failed after 1.4s: Exception Failed to connect to browser'. The dummy proxy recorded b'GET http://127.0.0.1:57639/json/version HTTP/1.1' four times, so zendriver's DevTools discovery request went through the env proxy. Fix idea: build an opener with urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}). Note: pyproject allows websockets>=14.0, and websockets>=15 also reads env proxies for ws://, so the CDP socket will hit the same problem on upgrade.

findings.title: Browser.get always raises TimeoutError when autodiscover_targets=False, even though navigation succeeded
findings.scenario: `b = await zd.start(autodiscover_targets=False)` (Config accepts it through kwargs; tests use config.autodiscover_targets=False). Then `await b.get(url)` or `await b.get(url, new_tab=True)`. get() only finishes when the browser connection receives Target.targetInfoChanged for the tab. Those events are only delivered after Target.setDiscoverTargets(discover=True), which start() sends only when autodiscover_targets is True. So every Browser.get waits the full timeout (10s by default) and raises TimeoutError, even though Page.navigate or createTarget has already completed. Tab.get(new_tab=True) is affected too, because it delegates to Browser.get. Tab.close() fails the same way: its TargetDestroyed wait times out after 10s (tab.py, outside this scope).
findings.why_tests_miss: The only test with autodiscover_targets=False (test_start_waits_for_initial_tab) checks len(browser.tabs) and never calls get().
findings.repro_idea: cfg = zd.Config(headless=True); cfg.autodiscover_targets = False; b = await zd.start(cfg); then time `await b.get('data:text/html,hi', timeout=3)` and `await b.get('data:text/html,two', new_tab=True, timeout=3)`.
findings.evidence: Probe scratchpad/detect-A4/nodisc_probe.py printed 'get(data url) autodiscover off: TimeoutError after 3.01s' and 'get(new_tab) autodiscover off: TimeoutError after 3.02s'. Right after, b.tabs showed both tabs already at their new URLs, so navigation had succeeded. 'close tab2: TimeoutError after 10.00s'.

findings.title: update_targets never removes destroyed targets, so browser.tabs, main_tab and get() keep using closed tabs
findings.scenario: update_targets only adds targets or updates them in place; it never drops entries missing from Target.getTargets. Removal happens only in the TargetDestroyed event handler, so whenever that event is not delivered, closed tabs stay in browser.targets forever. That is always the case with autodiscover_targets=False, where update_targets is the only way to sync. Example: start with autodiscover_targets=False, open a second tab, close the first tab, then call `await browser.update_targets()`. browser.tabs still lists the dead tab first, main_tab returns it, and `await browser.get(url)` navigates tabs[0], failing immediately with ProtocolException 'No target with given id found'. get_tab(), tile_windows() and CookieJar can also pick the dead tab.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test closes a tab and then checks browser.tabs after update_targets. Every test except one runs with autodiscover on, where the event handler hides the problem.
findings.repro_idea: Start with autodiscover_targets=False. Send Target.createTarget, then update_targets. Close the first tab with Target.closeTarget, then update_targets again. Compare browser.tabs with Target.getTargets, and call browser.get(url).

findings.title: Browser.get raises TimeoutError for navigations that never commit (204 No Content, downloads), while Tab.get returns normally
findings.scenario: `await browser.get('https://host/file.zip')`, where the server answers with Content-Disposition: attachment (or returns 204). Page.navigate completes without committing a new document, so Chrome emits no Target.targetInfoChanged with the new URL. wait_for_navigation never sees the target id, and get() raises TimeoutError after the full timeout (10s by default). Page.navigate itself only replies once the response arrives (measured at 2.01s against a server that waits 2s before answering), so the extra wait adds only this failure mode. Tab.get(url) returns normally in 0.11s for the same URL.

findings.title: grant_all_permissions always fails with ProtocolException on current Chromium
findings.scenario: `await browser.grant_all_permissions()` sends every cdp.browser.PermissionType value except CAPTURED_SURFACE_CONTROL in a single Browser.grantPermissions call. Chrome rejects the whole call if any single type is unknown or cannot be granted without an origin. On Chromium 141 (Linux) the call fails with 'Unknown permission type: localNetwork', and no permission is granted. Granting each type alone showed that localNetwork and loopbackNetwork are unknown to this Chromium. handTracking, protectedMediaIdentifier, smartCard and webPrinting are rejected with "Permissions can't be granted in current context." Those four fail even on a Chrome that knows every type, so the method cannot succeed on Linux. The CDP enum was regenerated in April 2026 (#254) and added types that the single exclusion does not cover.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test calls grant_all_permissions (grep over tests/ finds nothing).
findings.repro_idea: b = await zd.start(headless=True); await b.grant_all_permissions(). Then loop over cdp.browser.PermissionType, granting one at a time, to list which types are rejected.

findings.title: tile_windows only ever uses about one third of the screen width
findings.scenario: `await browser.tile_windows()` with the default max_columns=0 sets req_cols = int(n * 19/6), about 3.17n columns, and req_rows = 1 for any n >= 1. Each window gets screen_width / (3.17n) of width, so the n windows together always fill about 1/3 of the screen: 1 window gets 639px of 1920, 2 windows get 319px each, and 4 windows get 159px each (narrower than Chrome's minimum window width). The rest of the screen stays empty, and windows never get a second row.

findings.repro_idea: Stub sys.modules['mss'] with a fake reporting one 1920x1080 monitor. Stub tab.get_window and tab.set_window_size on n fake tabs, then print the grid returned by browser.tile_windows(tabs) for n = 1, 2 and 4.

The formula comes unchanged from upstream nodriver, so maintainers might call it intended, but it never tiles the screen.

findings.title: tile_windows raises ZeroDivisionError when there are no tabs, and leaks an mss instance (X display connection) on every call
findings.scenario: (a) `await browser.tile_windows()` (or windows=[]) on a browser with no page tabs: num_windows=0, so req_cols = 0 or int(0) = 0, and `req_rows = int(num_windows / req_cols)` raises ZeroDivisionError instead of returning []. (b) Every call creates `m = mss.mss()` and never closes it. mss 10 has no __del__; on Linux, MSS.__init__ calls XOpenDisplay, which only close() releases. findings.title: _register_handlers reuses its enabled_domains snapshot after a nested send changed it, so tab.send raises ValueError

findings.title: Expert mode: concurrent first sends inject the attachShadow override twice, so shadow DOM recurses until the stack overflows
findings.bug_class: check-then-await race (one-shot init flag set after await)

findings.title: expect_request/expect_response: buffered matching events overwrite request_id, so .response and .response_body come from a different request than .value
findings.bug_class: fire-and-forget handler tasks racing on shared state
findings.scenario: async with tab.expect_request(r'.*/pix\d+\.gif') as exp: await tab.get(page_with_30_images); req = await exp.value; resp = await exp.response. Chrome sends several Network.requestWillBeSent frames in one read. On Python >= 3.12, Listener.listener_loop drains buffered websocket frames without yielding: wait_for no longer creates a task, and websockets' SimpleQueue.get does not suspend when data is queued. So it calls asyncio.create_task(_request_handler(ev)) once per matching event before the first task runs and removes the handler. The first task sets request_future to request R1. Every later task overwrites self.request_id with its own id (Rn), and its request_future.set_result raises InvalidStateError inside an unobserved task. _response_handler then matches Rn. The result: exp.value / exp.request describe pix0.gif, while exp.response, exp.response_body and loading_finished_future describe pix9.gif (for example). BaseFetchInterception._response_handler and DownloadExpectation._handler have the same unguarded set_result, which produces the lost InvalidStateError tasks.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_expect_request and test_expect_response (tests/core/test_tab.py:417-443) use an exact URL that matches exactly one request, so a second matching handler task is never queued.
findings.repro_idea: Serve a page that loads 30 small images. Use a pattern that matches all of them. Assert (await exp.value).request_id == (await exp.response_future).request_id, and that no 'Task exception was never retrieved' is logged.
findings.evidence: probe_expect.py on real Chromium with Python 3.13: 5/5 trials mismatched. Sample: 'value.url=pix0.gif request_id(attr)=28835.11 value.request_id=28835.2 response.url=pix9.gif match=False'. The loop exception handler caught 55 lost InvalidStateError('invalid state') task exceptions.

findings.title: Sync event handlers run in worker threads, so the documented feed_cdp() from a sync handler raises RuntimeError and the paused request hangs
findings.bug_class: sync callback in thread touching asyncio objects
findings.scenario: tab.add_handler(cdp.fetch.RequestPaused, lambda ev, t: t.feed_cdp(cdp.fetch.continue_request(request_id=ev.request_id))); await tab.send(cdp.fetch.enable()); await tab.send(cdp.page.navigate(url)). Listener.listener_loop runs non-coroutine callbacks through asyncio.create_task(asyncio.to_thread(callback, *args)) (connection.py:1002), so the lambda runs in thread 'asyncio_0', which has no event loop. feed_cdp calls asyncio.ensure_future(self.send(...)), and that raises 'RuntimeError: There is no current event loop in thread asyncio_0' on 3.10 through 3.13. The error is lost in the unobserved to_thread task ('Task exception was never retrieved'), the send coroutine is never awaited, and Fetch.continueRequest is never sent. The paused request stays paused and the navigation hangs. feed_cdp's docstring says it is the non-async way to answer cdp.fetch.RequestPaused and stresses that it is 'not an async method, just a regular method', which is the sync-handler case. Any other sync handler that touches the loop (asyncio.Event.set, Future.set_result, create_task) is likewise unsafe from that thread.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test calls feed_cdp (grep finds nothing in tests/). The only sync handlers in tests are `lambda _: None` (test_tab.py:530, 556, 567), which never touch asyncio. examples/fetch_domain.py uses an async handler.
findings.repro_idea: With real Chromium, add a sync RequestPaused handler that calls tab.feed_cdp(continue_request), enable Fetch, navigate with a timeout, and assert that navigation completes. Compare with the async-handler version, which works.

findings.title: Connection.wait() / await tab / Tab.get hang forever when the listener is cancelled while waiting for idle
findings.bug_class: awaiting an Event owned by state another task replaces or kills
findings.scenario: A task runs `await tab` or `await tab.wait()` (Tab.get(url) also ends in self.wait()) while the page is busy, so idle is clear. Then the tab's session goes away: the tab is closed (Target.closeTarget, window.close(), or tab.close() from another task), or the browser websocket closes. The browser listener calls session._detach_session(), which cancels the session Listener, and on ConnectionClosed the listener just breaks out of its loop. A cancelled listener never sets its `idle` Event again, and wait() does `await self.listener.idle.wait()` on that dead listener's Event with no timeout and no done check. The coroutine stays pending forever instead of returning or raising.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test calls wait()/await tab while the target or connection goes away. test_connection.py has only test_concurrent_sends_open_a_single_websocket. wait_for_ready_state's hang test (test_tab.py:401) monkeypatches evaluate and never touches Listener.idle.
findings.repro_idea: Real Chromium: add a ConsoleAPICalled handler and start a ~1s console.log interval. Start asyncio.create_task(tab.wait()). After 0.3s send Target.closeTarget for the tab. Assert the waiter finishes within a few seconds. Control case without the close returns after about 1.1s.

findings.title: A session detached during send()'s awaits leaves _prep_headless_done set (HeadlessChrome UA leaks after reattach) and starts a zombie Listener
findings.scenario: Headless browser, first send on a tab: await tab.evaluate('1'). send() -> aopen() attaches the session -> _prepare_headless awaits _send_oneshot(Network.setUserAgentOverride). Meanwhile the session is detached: another task calls tab.aclose(), or the target detaches. _detach_session pops _prep_headless_done and fails the pending oneshot. _send_oneshot swallows that ProtocolException, and _prepare_headless then unconditionally runs setattr(self, '_prep_headless_done', True) for a session that no longer exists. On the next send the tab reattaches to a new session, and _prepare_headless skips the override, so navigator.userAgent and the UA header contain 'HeadlessChrome'. Back in the first send, line 642 `if not self.listener or not self.listener.running: self.listener = Listener(self)` sees the cancelled listener is done and starts a new Listener on the detached connection (websocket None, _inbox None). That listener dies at once with an unobserved ValueError('no websocket connection'). The tx already added to self.mapper at line 648 is then abandoned by the raise at line 658, and later surfaces as 'Transaction exception was never retrieved'. _prepare_expert (line 805) has the same flag-after-await pattern.
findings.why_tests_miss: tests/core/test_headless_user_agent.py checks the UA on a normally attached tab. No test detaches a session while its first send is still inside _prepare_headless and then checks the UA after reattach, and no test looks for listeners started on a detached connection.

Then check tab.evaluate('navigator.userAgent') for 'HeadlessChrome'. For the zombie listener, record Listener.__init__ calls made while conn.websocket is None.

ValueError(no websocket connection)'. probe_zombie.py (tab closed during its first send): 10/10 iterations created a Listener on a detached connection at connection.py:643 in send, with 9 unretrieved ValueError task exceptions. findings.title: _attach_session registers the session only after the attach reply, so a detachedFromTarget in the same batch is dropped and every later send on the tab hangs
findings.scenario: tab.send(...) on a target that is being destroyed: for example an OOPIF from get_frames() whose iframe is removed, or a tab closed concurrently. aopen -> _attach_session awaits browser_connection.send(Target.attachToTarget). Chrome sends the attach reply and then Target.detachedFromTarget for the new session. On Python >= 3.12 the browser listener handles both buffered frames before _attach_session resumes. _receive_message finds no entry in _sessions for that id, so the detach is ignored. Then _attach_session registers browser_connection._sessions[sid] = self and keeps session_id=sid. Every later command on the tab goes out with the dead sessionId. Chrome's reply for an unknown session carries no sessionId (verified against real Chromium: {"id":4,"error":{"code":-32001,"message":"Session with given id not found."}}). The reply is therefore routed to the browser connection, whose mapper does not contain the id, and silently dropped. tab.send has no timeout of its own, so this send and every later send on that tab hang forever.
findings.why_tests_miss: tests/core/test_frames.py and test_tab.py attach only to live targets. No test makes the detach arrive in the same batch as the attach reply, and none sends after Chrome has detached a session.
findings.repro_idea: A fake CDP server (websockets.serve) replies to Target.attachToTarget with {sessionId:'S1'}, sends detachedFromTarget for S1 immediately, and answers any message with a sessionId by an error without a sessionId, as Chrome does. Use a browser Connection plus a target Connection whose _owner.connection is it, then wait_for(tab.send(runtime.evaluate('1')), 3). It times out. With a 0.2s delay before the detach, it raises 'target session was detached' as it should.

(1) A per-content-document DOM.querySelectorAll that fails (stale id after another getDocument, or the iframe document being swapped) hits `except Exception as e: print(f'Exception in new content doc ids loop {e}')`: the error goes to stdout and those matches are dropped. (2) When the main-document query is stale, the retry calls `self.query_selector_all(selector, doc, ...)` with `_node=doc`, and content_doc_nodes are collected only when `not _node`, so the retry ignores all iframes. In both cases the main-document matches make `items` non-empty, so select_all/select return immediately with an incomplete list and never retry. Running 6 select_all('div', include_frames=True) concurrently gave 6 one-element lists.
findings.why_tests_miss: The include_frames unit test mocks send with ids that never go stale. No test runs queries concurrently or checks that the stdout is clean.
findings.repro_idea: Page with div#top and a same-origin iframe holding div#inner; res = await asyncio.gather(*(tab.select_all('div', include_frames=True) for _ in range(6))); every len(r) is 1, not 2, and 'Exception in new content doc ids loop Could not find node with given id' is printed. Probe: scratchpad/detect-A5/probe4.py.
findings.evidence: Probe: 'lens [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]' for the concurrent calls against '[sequential select_all ...] -> [<div id="top">..., <div id="inner">...]'. Stdout showed three 'Exception in new content doc ids loop Could not find node with given id ... DOM.querySelectorAll' lines. The same print also appears on a plain select('#inner', include_frames=True) right after page load.

findings.title: xpath(timeout=0) (or any timeout <= 0) never runs the query and always returns []; otherwise it busy-loops with no sleep
findings.scenario: `await tab.xpath("//p[@id='topp']", timeout=0)` returns [] although the element exists. The loop condition `(loop.time() - start_time) < timeout and len(items) == 0` is checked before the first attempt, so with timeout <= 0 the body never runs. The docstring says retries happen only 'if not immediately found', implying at least one attempt. With a positive timeout the loop has no sleep between attempts (find_all(timeout=0) raises immediately, the exception is caught, and the loop spins). findings.title: set_download_path / download_file / expect_download ignore the tab's browser context, so they do nothing for tabs from Browser.create_context()
findings.scenario: `ctx_tab = await browser.create_context(url)`, then `await ctx_tab.set_download_path(d)`, then clicking a download link. Browser.setDownloadBehavior is sent without browser_context_id. Chrome then applies it to the DEFAULT browser context, not the context the tab belongs to. The download is not saved to d (or anywhere). DownloadExpectation.__aenter__/__aexit__ use the same call, so `async with ctx_tab.expect_download() as ex: click(); await ex.value` never gets DownloadWillBegin and hangs. Meanwhile those calls change the download behaviour of the default context (other tabs) instead.

findings.title: Download path is tracked per Tab but set browser-wide, so download_file on a second tab silently moves every download to ./downloads

findings.title: download_file puts url and filename into JS string literals without escaping; a quote or backslash makes it silently do nothing
findings.scenario: `await tab.download_file(url, "O'Reilly.txt")` (or a URL containing ', or a Windows PathLike filename with backslashes such as 'sub\\x.txt') builds `_downloadFile('%s', '%s')` with the raw values. findings.title: Tab defines __eq__ without __hash__, so Tab objects are unhashable
findings.scenario: Defining __eq__ in Tab sets Tab.__hash__ = None (Connection, the parent class, is hashable). `set(browser.tabs)`, `{tab: result}`, a WeakKeyDictionary, or an lru_cache keyed on a tab all raise `TypeError: unhashable type: 'Tab'`. __eq__ also compares the whole mutable TargetInfo snapshot (url, title, attached...) rather than target_id, so a hash built on it could not be stable anyway. The natural fix is __eq__/__hash__ based on target_id.

findings.title: wait_for_ready_state uses equality, so the default until='interactive' times out on a page that is already 'complete'
findings.scenario: tab = await browser.get(fast_url); await tab.wait_for_ready_state() (default until='interactive'). Browser.get returns once navigation starts, and a fast page is already 'complete' by the first poll. _poll checks `ready_state == until`. 'complete' never equals 'interactive' and readyState never goes backwards, so the call polls for the full timeout and then raises TimeoutError('time ran out while waiting for load page until interactive'), even though the page passed 'interactive' long ago. until='loading' fails the same way on any page that is no longer loading.

No test calls the default or 'interactive'.

findings.title: find/find_all/find_elements_by_text crash with AttributeError when matching text is inside a shadow root in a same-origin iframe (including the user-agent shadow DOM of <input placeholder>)
findings.scenario: The page has a same-origin iframe (srcdoc or same-origin src) containing <input placeholder='Search needle'> or an element with an open shadow root holding the text. Calling await tab.find('needle'), tab.find_all('needle'), tab.wait_for(text='needle') or tab.find_elements_by_text('needle') reaches the iframe branch, which calls util.filter_recurse_all(iframe_elem, pred). Called on an Element, filter_recurse_all yields Element children, but for children that have shadow roots it recurses into child.shadow_roots[0], a raw cdp.dom.Node, and appends raw cdp Nodes to the result. Line 765 then evaluates `element.create(text_node.node, ...)` on a cdp.dom.Node and raises AttributeError: 'Node' object has no attribute 'node'. find() and find_all() do not catch it, so the whole lookup fails, and keeps failing on every retry.
findings.why_tests_miss: The only iframe text-search test (tests/core/test_frames.py::test_find_with_include_frames_searches_cross_site_frames) uses cross-site out-of-process iframes. Those have no content_document in the main DOM tree, so the iframe branch is skipped. No test has a same-origin iframe that contains a shadow root or an input.

findings.title: Remote object handles from DOM.resolveNode are never released (unbounded growth per apply/click/update)
findings.scenario: Every apply(), click(), update(), select_option(), send_keys(), clear_input() and so on calls DOM.resolveNode without an objectGroup and never calls Runtime.releaseObject, and nothing in zendriver/core ever releases objects. Each call adds a new entry to the page's inspector object table, and the entry lives until the execution context is destroyed. A long-running automation that polls an element on a single-page app grows that table without bound.
findings.why_tests_miss: Tests are short-lived and never check renderer-side handle counts.
findings.repro_idea: probe6.py: 3000 inp.apply() calls, then count distinct object_ids and call Runtime.callFunctionOn on the very first id.
findings.evidence: probe6.py: '3000 apply() calls in 1.8s -> 3000 distinct object ids'; 'first object id still alive after 3000 calls: inp None', so the first handle is still valid. grep for release_object/object_group in zendriver/core finds nothing.

findings.title: copy.copy / copy.deepcopy / pickle of an Element crash with RecursionError

B15 bug class: exception and cancellation handling

findings.title: A command reply that fails to parse kills the Listener, and the send() waiting for it hangs forever (aclose() cannot release it either)
findings.bug_class: exception-handling / exception escapes a loop and hangs a caller
findings.scenario: Any tab.send()/connection.send() whose result the generated cdp parser rejects. This happens when Chrome's protocol differs from the bundled cdp: a required key is missing (KeyError), or there is a new enum value, e.g. a cookie sameSite value unknown to CookieSameSite (ValueError). listener_loop pops the Transaction from conn.mapper and then calls tx(**message) outside any try. Inside Transaction.__call__, cdp_obj.send(result) raises something other than StopIteration, and the exception leaves listener_loop, so the listener task dies. The Future is never resolved. It is already gone from mapper, so _fail_pending_transactions in aclose()/_detach_session can never fail it, and send() hangs forever. Its own explicit `raise ProtocolException('could not parse the cdp response')` also kills the listener instead of failing the tx. On the browser connection this also starves every flat-session tab, because no one reads the websocket until another browser-level send() creates a new Listener. Event parsing on the same loop does catch these errors (parse_json_event in try/except -> logger.info; continue), which shows the intended behaviour.
findings.why_tests_miss: tests/core/test_connection.py has one test (concurrent aopen). No test feeds a malformed or schema-drifted reply. Real-Chrome tests use a Chrome that matches the bundled cdp.
findings.repro_idea: Run a fake websockets.serve peer that answers Target.getTargetInfo with {"id":N,"result":{}}. Call conn.send(cdp.target.get_target_info()) as a task, wait 3s, then call conn.aclose() and check that the task is still pending. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_tx_parse.py and probe_tx_parse2.py
findings.evidence: probe_tx_parse.py printed: 'send done within 3s: False | listener running: False | listener exc: KeyError('targetInfo')' with the task stuck at connection.py:662 `return await tx`. The same happened for Storage.getCookies with sameSite 'SomeFutureValue': listener exc ValueError("'SomeFutureValue' is not a valid CookieSameSite"). probe_tx_parse2.py: 'after aclose(): send finished? False | tx in mapper: 0'. The only trace is 'Task exception was never retrieved' at GC. Related to the known 'listener only catches Timeout/Cancelled/ConnectionClosed' lead, but this site is outside that try. The fix belongs in result dispatch (tx.set_exception), and the tx is lost permanently.

findings.title: Browser.stop() hangs forever on an unresponsive browser, because the CDP detach/close steps have no timeout and the terminate/kill fallback comes after them
findings.bug_class: cleanup path blocks forever / kill fallback unreachable
findings.scenario: The Chrome browser process stops responding (hung or suspended) and the user calls `await browser.stop()`. _stop first awaits `target.aclose()` for every target. For attached tabs that sends Target.detachFromTarget through the browser connection and awaits the reply with no timeout. Then it awaits `self.connection.send(cdp.browser.close())`, also with no timeout. The 3s terminate -> kill fallback is never reached, so stop() never returns. If the caller wraps it in wait_for, the cancellation leaves the process running and the profile undeleted.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_pending_commands_fail_when_browser_process_dies / ..._connection_is_closed suspend the process but call connection.aclose() and then resume or kill it. They never call browser.stop() while Chrome is unresponsive. test_browser_stop_exits_gracefully_without_kill uses a healthy browser.
findings.repro_idea: Start a headless browser and attach a tab (tab.evaluate('1')). Send SIGSTOP to browser._process.pid, then run `await asyncio.wait_for(browser.stop(), 10)`. It times out, and task.print_stack() shows it waiting on Target.detachFromTarget. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_stop_hang.py, probe_stop_hang2.py

findings.title: One event handler that raises when called (e.g. wrong arity) kills the Listener through an explicit re-raise, so commands already in flight hang
findings.scenario: A user registers `async def on_target(): ...` (no parameters) via browser.connection.add_handler(cdp.target.TargetCreated, on_target) or tab.add_handler(...). _accepts_connection_argument returns False, so the loop calls callback(event), which raises TypeError synchronously while the coroutine object is created. The dispatch block logs a warning and then `raise`s (the outer `except Exception: raise` passes it on too), so the listener task dies. The reply to a command that is already in flight, and is queued right behind the event, is never read: that send() hangs until some later send() happens to create a new Listener. Every other handler for every event also stops firing. On the browser connection this starves all flat-session tabs, since nothing reads the shared websocket.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test registers a handler whose signature does not fit. Handler tests use well-formed lambdas and coroutines.
findings.repro_idea: Run a fake CDP peer that, for Browser.getVersion, first sends a Target.targetCreated event and then the reply. Register a good handler plus `async def bad(): pass`, then call conn.send(cdp.browser.get_version()) with a 3s timeout. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-B15/probe_bad_handler.py
findings.evidence: probe_bad_handler.py printed: 'get_version finished within 3s: False' and 'listener running: False exc: TypeError('main.<locals>.bad_handler() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given')'. findings.title: Browser.__aexit__ and Connection/Tab.__aexit__ replace the user's exception with exc_type(exc_val): TypeError for multi-arg exceptions and ExceptionGroup, wrong exit status for sys.exit, and ProtocolException.code lost

When the body raises, __aexit__ runs `raise exc_type(exc_val)` instead of returning and letting Python re-raise. findings.title: Element.click() (and mouse_click/mouse_move/mouse_drag/flash/screenshot_b64) raises a bare Exception on display:none elements: get_position never returns None, so every 'not visible' fallback is dead code
findings.bug_class: wrong exception raised / caller's None-handling unreachable
findings.scenario: `btn = await tab.select('#hidden-button'); await btn.click()` on a display:none element, e.g. a hidden <input type=file> or a visually hidden checkbox. click() calls `await self.flash(0.25)` before the JS `el.click()`. flash() calls get_position(), and Chrome returns empty content quads, so get_position runs `raise Exception('could not find position ...')`. findings.title: Element.apply drops JavaScript exceptions: a throwing function returns None, and the exception_details branch is dead

findings.title: expect_request/expect_response: two matching requests in one burst cause InvalidStateError in a handler task and make .response/.response_body belong to a different request than .request
findings.bug_class: unhandled exception in handler task (set_result on done future) + state overwrite

findings.title: (Outside B15's bug class, found while reading) Tab.__call__ passes text and selector to wait_for in swapped positions, so tab(text=...) never finds text
findings.scenario: `await tab(text='Hello world')` calls `self.wait_for(text, selector, timeout)` positionally, but the signature is wait_for(selector=None, text=None, timeout=10). The text is used as a CSS selector ('Hello world' matches no element), the call polls for the full timeout and raises TimeoutError('time ran out while waiting') even though the text is on the page. tab(selector='button') only appears to work because DOM.performSearch also matches tag names.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test or doc calls the Tab object directly.

Every except/finally/raise in zendriver/core was grepped and triaged. Probes ran against real headless Chromium and fake websockets CDP peers on Python 3.13.16.
coverage.not_covered: I did not probe Python 3.10/3.11-specific behaviour: the asyncio.TimeoutError vs builtin TimeoutError split (cloudflare.verify_cf raises builtin TimeoutError while the rest of the library documents asyncio.TimeoutError), or the wait_for result/cancellation races in listener_loop on 3.10/3.11. I did not read config.py, keys.py or _contradict.py in depth (sync code, almost no exception handling). Not read: element.py send_keys/send_file/set_value and other methods, and tab.py download/print_to_pdf/get_all_urls. Leads I checked and dropped: verify_cf after the input disappears via document replacement (worked in the probe); the query_selector '__last' stale-node flag (could not trigger 'could not find node' because DOM.getDocument did not invalidate ids); the class-level Browser._update_target_info_mutex shared across event loops (its body never awaits, so it is never contended); strict utf-8 decode in _read_process_stderr masking the 'Failed to connect' error and skipping stop() (plausible but needs non-UTF-8 stderr, not shown). Lower-value items I did not report: DownloadExpectation/BaseFetchInterception __aexit__ sending CDP commands that can mask the body's exception; Tab.mouse_click without try/finally leaving the button pressed if cancelled between mouse_down and mouse_up; Connection.aclose not clearing enabled_domains when the listener has already died. Known-issue sites were skipped as instructed.
